introduction_markdown:
**GENERAL CERTIFICATE OF EDUCATION BOARD - General Certificate of Education Examination. JUNE 2025, ADVANCED LEVEL. English Language, Paper 2 (0730).**

Answer your questions either exclusively from **PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS)** or from **PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS)**.

**PART ONE (NEW SYLLABUS) - Duration: Two and a Quarter Hours.** Instructions to candidates: ANSWER ONE QUESTION FROM EACH SECTION (Section A: Composition, Section B: Prescribed Texts, Section C: Creative Writing). ALL QUESTIONS CARRY EQUAL MARKS. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - Duration: Three Hours.** Instructions to candidates: Answer BOTH questions in SECTION A and ONE EACH from SECTIONS B and C in the SAME Answer Booklet, beginning each section on a new page. Read all instructions on BOTH the question paper and the answer booklet very carefully. Failure to obey these instructions or to number your work as on the question paper will cause you to lose marks. Any unusual mark, sign or unnecessary disclosure of your identity will be considered as an attempt to cheat and will earn you a penalty. In the SUMMARY question, use mainly your own words. Indiscriminate copying of portions of the passage as your answer will earn you little or no marks. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. A pre-prepared or memorised composition will earn you little or no marks.

**PART TWO (OLD SYLLABUS) - SECTION B: COMPOSITION (20 marks)**

Mark distribution: Content and Organisation (06 marks); Expression (08 marks); Accuracy (06 marks).

Choose ONE topic to write about from the list below. You are advised to write clearly and effectively, to spell and punctuate correctly, and to ensure that your writing is appropriate in style and content to the topic chosen. Avoid obscene language and do not disclose your identity. You should write between 500 and 550 words.

questions.enonce_markdown: **d)** Depression is on the rise in our society today. What are the causes of this situation and what can be done to check it?
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Plan**

1. Introduction: what depression is and its rise.
2. Causes: economic hardship, breakdown of family ties.
3. Causes: pressure, social media, trauma, drugs; the problem of silence.
4. Solutions: break the silence, professional help, tackle root causes, friendship and community.
5. Conclusion.

**Model composition (521 words)**

Depression is a serious mental illness in which a person feels deep sadness, hopelessness and a loss of interest in life for weeks or months. In our society today, more and more people, including young students, suffer from it, and some even end their lives. This alarming rise calls for an understanding of its causes and for urgent action to check it.

Several causes can be identified. The first is economic hardship. Many graduates remain jobless for years, parents cannot pay school fees, and the high cost of living leaves families in permanent anxiety. A person who feels that he can never provide for himself or his children may lose hope. The second cause is the breakdown of family and social ties. In the past, the extended family and the neighbourhood shared problems, but today many people live alone, or in homes where parents are too busy to listen to their children. Loneliness is fertile ground for depression.

Another cause is the pressure of modern life. Students are pushed to obtain top marks and are humiliated when they fail; young people compare themselves with the glamorous lives displayed on social media and conclude that they are worthless. Cyberbullying adds to the harm. Traumatic events, such as the death of a loved one, insecurity, displacement from one's home, abuse or the loss of a business, can also cause severe depression, especially when no support is offered. Drug and alcohol abuse, which many use to escape their sorrows, makes the condition worse.

Unfortunately, silence and ignorance aggravate the problem. Many people think that depression is weakness, witchcraft or a lack of faith, and sufferers are afraid to speak out. As a result, they do not receive treatment until it is too late.

What can be done to check it? First, we must break the silence. Families, schools, churches and the media should teach that depression is an illness and not a shame, and that it can be treated. Parents should listen to their children, spend time with them and notice changes such as withdrawal, loss of appetite or sleeplessness.

Second, professional help must be provided. Hospitals and schools should employ psychologists and counsellors, and the government should train more mental health workers and make consultations affordable. A person in crisis should be encouraged to contact a doctor or a telephone helpline without fear of judgement.

Third, we must tackle the root causes. The authorities should create jobs, support small businesses and help poor families so that fewer people live in despair. Schools should reduce unnecessary pressure and punish bullying, while young people should use social media wisely and remember that the pictures they see are rarely the whole truth.

Finally, each of us can be a friend. A kind word, a visit or an invitation to share a meal can save a life. Religious and community groups can offer a place of belonging, and activities such as sport and music give people joy and purpose.

In conclusion, depression is rising because of pressure, hardship and loneliness, but it can be checked if we talk about it, treat it and care for one another.

**Marking grid (the paper prints the split of the 20 marks)**

| Criterion | Marks | What earns the marks |
|---|---|---|
| Content and Organisation | 6 | A relevant treatment of the topic as set, a clear introduction, paragraphs that each develop one idea, a logical order and a conclusion |
| Expression | 8 | Varied sentence structures, precise vocabulary, suitable register and tone, good use of linking words, a convincing style |
| Accuracy | 6 | Correct grammar, spelling and punctuation |

**Common mistakes**

1. Writing fewer than 500 or more than 550 words, or ignoring the topic's exact wording (for example listing points instead of telling a story, or giving only one side when asked 'Do you agree?').
2. A weak plan: a long introduction, paragraphs that repeat one idea, no conclusion; or a pre-prepared composition that does not fit the question (it earns no marks).
3. Giving the causes only, or the remedies only: the question has two parts ('causes' and 'what can be done'), and both must be developed.
